brief.headline: Push payment to 30 days and free up ₹2.25 L in cash; hold pricing at current in exchange for faster turns.

priceAsk.summary: Hold current pricing stable — market shows these caps trade at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, which is market-fair territory.
priceAsk.target: No cut sought; anchor at ₹0.85–0.95/pc market typical
priceAsk.basis: The market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, verdict MARKET-FAIR. Our spend is ₹27.42 L annually, so locking in today's rate while we shorten payment keeps the deal balanced.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days after receipt.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹2.25 L in cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: This supplier publishes no financials, so we don't know their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we build our plan around our own data and lining up a second source. Our ₹27.42 L annual spend is meaningful to a mid-sized packaging converter, and the market shows five robust alternates — three listed firms and Manjushree Technopack (India's largest rigid-plastic converter, revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B). With credible backup options ready, we can confidently ask for faster payment terms without risking supply, even though we're flying blind on their balance sheet.

evidence.point: We spend ₹27.42 L a year with them on rigid plastic packaging.
Shortening payment from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹2.25 L in cash for us.
Market asking prices for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc, and the verdict is MARKET-FAIR — modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec.
HDPE resin import unit value sits at 87.61 ₹/kg, giving us a raw-material cost benchmark.
Manjushree Technopack, India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, has revenue of ₹2569.83 Cr and a health score of B — a strong second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter, revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health B; pharma bottles, caps and preforms are their core — top second-source fit.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging; strong and profitable — robust alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd (a lead to qualify — verify before RFQ)
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging firm; broad capability across bottles and caps.

risks: Their financials aren't public, so we can't gauge cash health or how hard to push — plan assumes they're stable but confirms we need a qualified second source before pressing further.

We're not their worst payment terms (45 days after receipt), so they may push back on moving to 30 — frame it as a mutual win (faster cash for them, freed-up working capital for us) rather than a unilateral demand.
Market pricing is already fair (₹0.85–0.95/pc typical), so asking for a cut risks souring the relationship for marginal gain — better to lock current rates and improve terms.

The alternates listed are leads from web research, not qualified or priced — before leaning hard on supplier switching, we must RFQ and audit at least one to confirm they can match spec, capacity and price.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership and want to keep volumes steady — can we look at moving payment to 30 days to help both our cash cycles, while we lock in current pricing for the year?
